sentences.text:
The appellants have averred that on 26.06.2018, Ms. Jiji Marry Johnson, Food Safety Officer (FSO), took sample of "Besan (Tata Sampann)" from Sh. Arun Goyal, FBO-cum-Proprietor of M/s Goyal Store, 101-A, Sarojani Park, Shastri Nagar, Delhi - 110031, for analysis under the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 and after analysis, declared the said sample to be misbranded vide report dated 06.07.2018, opining that the declaration "Low Oil Absorb Besan" is misleading and likely to create erroneous impression regarding its character and same is in violation of Regulation No.
2.2.1.3 read with 2.3.1.5 of the Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labeling) Regulations 2011.

Consequently, a complaint was filed by the FSO against the appellant and others, before the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer, ADM (East), Shastri Nagar, Delhi and after considering the reply and rejoinder as well as the submissions made by both the parties, the A.O. / ADM, vide impugned order dated 03.10.2023, imposed a penalty of Rs. 20,000/- on appellant no. 1 Arun Goyal, penalty of Rs.
50,000/- on Sh. Sumit Katyal, penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/- each on appellants no. 3 to 5, penalty of Rs.
1,50,000/- on Sh. Madan Lal and penalty of Rs. 2,00,000/- on appellant no. 6 Tata Chemicals Ltd.,
Mumbai.
Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order dated 03.10.2023, the present appeal has been filed for adjudication.

13. The right to be heard is one of the fundamental principles of natural justice, which is to be followed by all the Administrative Authorities and Quasi Judicial Authorities.

i. Judicial or even quasi- judicial opinions these days can be as different as the judges and authorities who deliver them.
All these decisions serve one common purpose which is to demonstrate by reason that the relevant factors have been objectively considered.

j. Insistence on reason is a requirement for both judicial accountability and transparency.
